guarantees.claim: When hmac_en changes value, in_process and initiated are both low.
When wipe_secret is high, in the next clock cycle secret_key equals the wipe_v value replicated to fill the width of secret_key.
After reset, intr_hmac_done_o is a known value (not X).
After reset, intr_fifo_empty_o is a known value.
After reset, tl_o.d_valid is a known value.
After reset, tl_o.a_ready is a known value.
After reset, alert_tx_o is a known value.
If a write to u_reg has more than one bit set in its write enable (non-one-hot), an error is triggered and alert_tx_o[0] is asserted.

uncertain_points.claim: The assertion requires that secret_key is updated to the wipe_v pattern in the next cycle after wipe_secret. Verify that the actual sequential RTL logic for secret_key implements exactly this clearing behavior.
uncertain_points.risk: If the implementation uses a different clearing value or timing, secret data may not be fully wiped, leaving sensitive key material.

uncertain_points.claim: The assertion requires that hmac_en changes only when both in_process and initiated are low. Confirm that the state machine logic enforces this condition under all operational modes.
uncertain_points.risk: A violation could indicate a state machine bug causing HMAC operation during an active transaction, potentially leading to data corruption or security bypass.
